names.note: Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 5 марта ст. ст., name page 9620, «Иоанн (Миротворцев), иерей, сщмч.», with the grade and rank words left off; the day’s own line gives the forename declined and no surname at all. `.tmp/foldchk.py` and `.tmp/rusurn.py` were run over the form and over the surname, and the gate’s own `nameKeys` over the proposed folder: no folder in the corpus holds this form, the surname returns nothing at all, and the proposed folder folds with nobody in either script.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 марта ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Иоанна пресвитера и прмчч. Мардария и Феофана (1938).»

attestations.note: **The line puts three men together and they are not a company.** It names a presbyter and then, under a second grade word, two monastics, and closes with one year for all three; the three lives read on azbyka.ru give three deaths on one day in three places — a camp in the Komi country, a shooting near Углич and a camp at Каргополь — and not one of the three names either of the others. Sharing a day is not a relation, so no `related` row is written for any of them. azbyka.ru gives him four synaxes besides this day — of the New Martyrs, of the Komi saints, of the Rostov and Yaroslavl saints and of the Saratov saints — all of which were seen and none of which was read or recorded as a feast.

birth.note: azbyka.ru, out of игумен Дамаскин (Орловский), «Жития новомучеников и исповедников Российских ХХ века. Март»: «Священномученик Иоанн родился 25 марта 1881 года в селе Елшанка Саратовского уезда Саратовской губернии в семье крестьянина Николая Миротворцева». days.pravoslavie.ru gives no year of birth.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru closes the line for 5 марта ст. ст. with «(1938)», which it gives to all three of that line. azbyka.ru: «Священник Иоанн Миротворцев скончался в Ухтпечлаге 18 марта 1938 года и был погребен в безвестной могиле» — and the civil 18 March 1938 is this Julian 5 March. He was not shot: the ten-year sentence ran out in the camp.
